column1: # The store-write hypothesis, as four configurations of the SAME program.
# All four fix --threads 32 so that thread count cannot explain a difference,
# and compare.sh deletes each store before its run, so every one of them starts
# cold: the only thing that varies is what the run does with the disk.
#   normal        writes the store, on real disk -- the thing to explain
#   nowritecache  reads a store, writes nothing. If the disk is the ceiling,
#                 THIS is the run that recovers the missing CPU. If it does
#                 not, the write path is not where the CPU went.
#   nocache       no reads, no writes, recompute everything. Not a clean
#                 control (it changes three things at once, see
#                 ReadOnlyStorageBackend) but it bounds the store's total cost.
#   sparse        the store's own low-write mode, for scale between the two.
